doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why he loves the valve trombone
summary: He likes the valve trombone's trombone quality with trumpet-like fingering, and notes Brookmeyer and Raul de Souza, while slide players call it cheating.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: What do you love about the valve trombone?
That is what I have, the quality of the trombone with the feeling of the trumpet. The [imitates sound] You can feel the finger, because it’s a finger instrument.
So you like the way the valve trombone is manipulated?

Yea. I love that instrument for many, many years. The way that wanting soul, or bump intervals in place and Raul DeSouza played the slide trombone and also the valve trombone; I know he played the valve trombone.
And Bob Brookmeyer, very few. In the history of Jazz have been very few, Billy Eckstine used to play valve trombone.
My father-in-law was an ex-trombone player. He refers to the valve trombone as cheating .
Oh, yea, yea. Trombonists they don’t like that. [Both laugh]
It’s like playing the clarinet with covered holes; that is the same thing. No serious clarinet player would play with a covered hole clarinet.
